newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World Bank says Bangladesh bridge not harmful.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says Bangladesh bridge not harmful.

text.p: A major bridge under construction in Bangladesh, which would link the country's eastern and western districts, will not harm the environment or local villages, the World Bank said on Tuesday.

Enough measures had been taken to prevent damaging effects on the environment and local residents from the 4.8 km (2.9-mile) bridge, which would straddle the Jamuna river, World Bank officials in Dhaka said.
The Bank had earlier appointed an inspection panel to investigate whether the bridge would have a negative effect on more than 70,000 people living on 75 islands on the river.
The Bank's executive directors accepted the panel's recommendation that a further investigation into the Jamuna Bridge Project "was not warranted at this time", the Bank said.
A local pressure group had pushed for a further probe into possible damaging effects from the bridge.
The World Bank, Asian Development Bank and Japan are providing $200 million each for the bridge, which is due to be completed by the middle of 1998.
Bangladesh expects the bridge, which will be the country's longest, to provide key links between eastern and western parts of the country, spurring economic growth.
